questions.q: Sort each concern about a new technology by the kind of impact it is.
items: Is it right to collect this data at all?
Does this break the Data Protection Act?
Will people without internet access be left out?
How much electricity will the data centre use?
Should a machine decide who gets a loan?
Who owns the copyright in what it produces?
questions.feedback: Ethical is about right and wrong; legal is about what the law says. They often point the same way, but they are different questions.

questions.q: Explain the difference between an ethical issue and a legal issue.

markPoints.concept: a legal issue is about what the law allows or forbids
markPoints.exemplar: A legal issue is about what the law allows or forbids.

markPoints.concept: an ethical issue is about what is right, whether or not it is legal
accept: whether or not|even if|even where|still|not illegal|perfectly legal|still legal|lawful|law permits|law allows|nothing to do with the law|regardless
markPoints.exemplar: An ethical issue is about whether something is right, even if the law allows it.

questions.example: A legal issue is about whether something breaks the law. An ethical issue is about whether it is right, which is a separate question — something can be perfectly legal and still be wrong.
questions.paraphrase: A legal issue concerns what legislation permits or prohibits. An ethical issue concerns whether an action is morally acceptable, which can differ even where nothing illegal has happened.
questions.feedback: Both halves, and the second one needs the idea that legal and right are not the same thing.

questions.q: State what is meant by a stakeholder.

markPoints.concept: anybody affected by the decision or the technology

questions.example: Anybody affected by a decision or a piece of technology, such as the users, the workers, the company and the people living nearby.
questions.paraphrase: Any person or group with an interest in or affected by what is decided.
questions.feedback: Affected by it. Naming examples without saying what they have in common is not the definition.
